messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
The sentence is a rhetorical plea written in Early Modern English, characterized by archaic spellings and syntax. It appeals to the listener's sense of duty and compassion regarding the speaker’s aging father. The core argument questions how one could abandon a parent who is suffering from blindness and poverty when the speaker has the means to provide comfort. This emotional appeal relies on the contrast between the father’s destitute state and the potential for a happy old age if care were given.

Consydre
thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?
